research.periodic_elements.uranium_oxide: Roast pitchblende for the black oxide Klaproth named uranium
research.periodic_elements.flintlock.des: A steel-barrelled musket fired by flint: harder hitting and quicker to reload than the hand cannon
research.periodic_elements.dynamo.desc: A self-exciting dynamo driven by a steam engine: current by the kilowatt, carried on copper wire (Siemens 1866)
research.periodic_elements.bessemer.desc: Blow air through molten pig iron: its own carbon burns and keeps it molten; steel by the tonne
Electrolyse brine over a mercury cathode: lye, chlorine and hydrogen (Castner and Kellner)
research.periodic_elements.air_liquefact: Compress and cool air until it is liquid, then boil off nitrogen, argon and oxygen in turn (Linde)
Every element colours a flame with its own lines: a prism finds traces no balance can (Bunsen and Kirchhoff)
research.periodic_elements.electrolytic_: Refine copper by current; the slime under the anodes holds the precious metals and tellurium
Dissolve alumina in molten cryolite and split it with current: aluminium becomes cheaper than silver
research.periodic_elements.noble_gases.d: Boil liquid air slowly and read each fraction in the spectroscope (Ramsay and Travers)
research.periodic_elements.rubidium_caes: The first elements found by spectrum: in the lithium liquor of pegmatite
research.periodic_elements.indium.desc: An indigo line in zinc ore: catch indium in the retort flue dust
research.periodic_elements.germanium.des: Mendeleev's eka-silicon, found where he said it would be; reduce its oxide with hydrogen (Winkler)
research.periodic_elements.thallium.desc: A bright green line in lead-chamber sludge (Crookes)
research.periodic_elements.platinum_meta: Part anode slime with aqua regia into platinum, palladium and rhodium; the black residue holds ruthenium, osmium and iridium
research.periodic_elements.bayer_process: Dissolve the alumina out of bauxite with hot lye under pressure and leave the iron behind as red mud
research.periodic_elements.gallium.desc: Draw gallium from the Bayer liquor: a metal that melts in your hand
research.periodic_elements.fluorine.desc: Hydrogen fluoride from fluorspar, electrolysed in platinum: the most reactive element, isolated at last (Moissan)
research.periodic_elements.manganese.des: Ferromanganese from pyrolusite; steel with 12% manganese grows harder where it is struck (Hadfield)
research.periodic_elements.solvay.desc: Soda ash from salt and limestone with ammonia as the go-between
research.periodic_elements.tungsten.desc: Tungsten from wolframite; Mushet's tungsten steel holds its edge when red hot
research.periodic_elements.vanadium.desc: Vanadium oxide from vanadinite; reduce it with burning aluminium (Roscoe; Goldschmidt)
research.periodic_elements.contact_proce: Sulfur dioxide over a hot catalyst: strong sulfuric acid by the tonne
Carbon monoxide carries nickel off as a gas and lays it down pure (Mond)
research.periodic_elements.radioactivity: Uranium salts discharge a gold-leaf electroscope through paper: invisible rays (Becquerel)
research.periodic_elements.helium.desc: The gas from uranium ore shows the yellow line seen only in the sun (Ramsay)
research.periodic_elements.radium.desc: Follow the activity through tonnes of pitchblende residue to a gram of radium (Marie and Pierre Curie)
research.periodic_elements.polonium.desc: The first element found by its radioactivity; named for Poland
research.periodic_elements.actinium.desc: Debierne's ray-giving element from the rare-earth part of the residue
research.periodic_elements.radon.desc: Radium gives off a radioactive gas: pump it off and seal it in gold seeds (Dorn)
research.periodic_elements.radiogenic_he: Radium sealed in a tube slowly fills it with helium: alpha rays are helium (Ramsay and Soddy, Rutherford)
research.periodic_elements.thorium.desc: Thorium from the black sand of beaches: dissolve its oxide and reduce the chloride with potassium (Berzelius)
research.periodic_elements.smokeless_pow: Guncotton gelled into a powder that burns without smoke and three times as strong (Vieille)
research.periodic_elements.breech_loadin: A steel rifle loaded from the back with brass cartridges of smokeless powder (Lebel)
research.periodic_elements.arc_furnace.d: Strike an arc between graphite electrodes: heat no fuel can give, for silicon and ferroalloys (Heroult 1900)
research.periodic_elements.haber_process: Bread from air: ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen at 200 atmospheres (Haber 1909, Bosch 1913)
research.periodic_elements.flotation.des: Pine oil and bubbles float sulfide grains away from the rock: ores too poor to smelt become worth mining
research.periodic_elements.stainless_ste: Steel with an eighth chromium does not rust (Brearley 1913)
research.periodic_elements.rare_earths.d: Crack monazite in acid and crystallize its salts again and again until the rare earths part (Auer von Welsbach)
research.periodic_elements.van_arkel.des: Grow pure zirconium on a hot wire from its iodide vapour (van Arkel and de Boer 1925)
research.periodic_elements.ostwald_proce: Burn ammonia on a platinum-rhodium gauze: nitric acid without saltpetre
research.periodic_elements.chromium.desc: Pure chromium from chromite: roast with soda and burn the green oxide with aluminium (Goldschmidt 1898)
research.periodic_elements.molybdenum.de: Roast molybdenite to its white oxide and reduce it with hydrogen (Hjelm 1781)
research.periodic_elements.rhenium.desc: The last stable element found, in the flue of a molybdenite roaster (Noddack, Tacke and Berg 1925)
research.periodic_elements.high_speed_st: Tool steel hardened from near melting cuts while red hot (Taylor and White 1900)
research.periodic_elements.cemented_carb: Tungsten carbide grains sintered in cobalt: wie Diamant (Widia 1926)
research.periodic_elements.beryllium_cop: Copper with 2% beryllium is as hard as steel and never sparks: tools for mines and powder works
research.periodic_elements.niobium.desc: Niobium parted from tantalum by crystallizing their fluoride salts (Marignac 1866)
research.periodic_elements.tantalum.desc: Ductile tantalum melted in the arc for lamp filaments (von Bolton 1903)
research.periodic_elements.didymium.desc: Didymium is two elements: green and pink salts after a hundred crystallizations (Auer von Welsbach 1885)
research.periodic_elements.hafnium.desc: X-ray lines showed a new element in every zircon; its fluoride crystallizes apart (Coster and Hevesy 1923)
The mother of actinium, found in pitchblende residue (Hahn and Meitner 1918)
research.periodic_elements.francium.desc: Element 87: a branch in actinium's decay, carried by caesium salt, gone within the hour (Perey 1939)
research.periodic_elements.geiger_counte: A gas tube that clicks for every ray: read radiation as you walk (Geiger and Muller 1928)
research.periodic_elements.kroll_process: Chlorinate the black sand, then strip the chlorine with magnesium under argon: titanium by the tonne (Kroll 1940)
Resin columns part in days the rare earths a century of crystallizing could not (Spedding 1947)
research.periodic_elements.crystal_growt: Grow one flawless crystal from the melt and sweep it clean: the stuff of transistors (Teal, Pfann)
research.periodic_elements.diamond_synth: Graphite in molten nickel squeezed to 50000 atmospheres becomes diamond (General Electric 1954)
research.periodic_elements.uranium_metal: Green salt reduced by magnesium in a sealed bomb: uranium for the first reactor (Ames 1942)
research.periodic_elements.titanium_allo: Titanium with 6% aluminium and 4% vanadium: netherite's strength, half the weight
research.periodic_elements.scandium.desc: Mendeleev's eka-boron, first made as metal in 1937 (Fischer)
research.periodic_elements.samarium_euro: Samarium from samarskite (Lecoq 1879) and europium split from it (Demarcay 1901)
research.periodic_elements.gadolinium_te: Gadolinium (Marignac 1880) and terbium, the second earth of Ytterby
research.periodic_elements.dysprosium_ho: Dysprosium, "hard to get at" (Lecoq 1886), and holmium for Stockholm (Cleve 1878)
research.periodic_elements.erbium_thuliu: Pink erbium and thulium for Thule (Cleve 1879)
research.periodic_elements.ytterbium_lut: The last rare earth found in nature, split from ytterbium (Urbain 1907)
research.periodic_elements.solar_cell.de: A silicon wafer turns sunlight straight into current (Bell Labs 1954)
research.periodic_elements.isotope_separ: Uranium-235 is 0.7% of uranium and chemically the same: only its lighter weight can part it (Oak Ridge 1945)
research.periodic_elements.nuclear_react: A pile of uranium and graphite went critical under a Chicago stand: neutrons split uranium faster than they escape (Fermi 1942)
Behind lead glass, spent fuel is dissolved and its uranium and plutonium pulled out by solvent (PUREX, Savannah River 1954)
research.periodic_elements.neptunium.des: The first element beyond uranium, made by neutrons on uranium (McMillan and Abelson 1940)
research.periodic_elements.technetium.de: The gap at 43 was filled by an element no ore holds: first from a cyclotron part, now by the kilogram from fission (Perrier and Segre 1937)
research.periodic_elements.promethium.de: The missing rare earth, found among the fission products of the Oak Ridge reactor (Marinsky, Glendenin and Coryell 1945)
research.periodic_elements.americium_cur: Plutonium soaked in neutrons gives americium, and americium gives curium (Seaborg, James, Morgan and Ghiorso 1944)
research.periodic_elements.cyclotron.des: Particles whirled in a magnet and kicked at every half turn reach millions of volts (Lawrence 1932): astatine was made in one (1940)
research.periodic_elements.berkelium_cal: Alpha particles on americium and curium gave elements 97 and 98, named for Berkeley and California (1949-50)
research.periodic_elements.mendelevium.d: Einsteinium from the first hydrogen bomb's debris, bombarded in the cyclotron one atom at a time (Ghiorso 1955)
research.periodic_elements.superconducto: Niobium-titanium wire cooled by liquid helium carries current with no loss: the magnets of every big accelerator and MRI scanner
research.periodic_elements.integrated_ci: A whole circuit printed on one chip of silicon (Kilby 1958, Noyce 1959): the start of the information age
research.periodic_elements.compound_semi: Gallium arsenide gives off light where silicon cannot: the first visible LED and the semiconductor laser (Holonyak 1962). The Heavy-Ion Accelerator needs its wafers
research.periodic_elements.electromagnet: Lawrence's calutrons bent uranium ions apart by mass at Oak Ridge; today they make rare isotopes such as calcium-48
research.periodic_elements.heavy_ion_acc: Whole nuclei, not just helium, fired at heavy targets: elements 102 and 103 at Berkeley and Dubna (1958-66)
research.periodic_elements.transactinide: Carbon, nitrogen and oxygen beams on californium gave elements 104 to 106 (Ghiorso, Berkeley 1969-74)
research.periodic_elements.cold_fusion.d: Gentle collisions of medium nuclei with lead and bismuth gave elements 107 to 113, one atom a week (GSI 1981-96, RIKEN 2004)
research.periodic_elements.hot_fusion.de: A calcium-48 beam on actinide targets reached the island of stability's shore: elements 114 to 118 (Oganessian, Dubna 1999-2010)
research.periodic_elements.permanent_mag: Neodymium, iron and boron make the strongest magnets (Sagawa 1984): direct-drive wind turbines with no gearbox
research.periodic_elements.composite_arm: Ceramic tiles shatter the bullet and woven aramid catches it: boron carbide plates over titanium (Kwolek's Kevlar 1965)
research.periodic_elements.complete_peri: IUPAC named the last four elements in 2016: the seventh row of the periodic table is full
research.periodic_elements.radioisotope_: Neptunium irradiated into plutonium-238, whose decay heat thermocouples turn into current for decades (Transit 4A 1961, Voyager 1977)
research.periodic_elements.smoke_detecto: A speck of americium ionises the air in a chamber; smoke stops the current and the alarm sounds (Duane Pearsall 1965)
research.periodic_elements.lithium_ion_b: Lithium ions shuttle between a cobalt oxide cathode and a carbon anode (Goodenough 1980, Yoshino 1985, Sony 1991)
research.periodic_elements.optical_fibre: Light in glass fibre amplified by erbium carries a world network (Kao 1966, Payne and Desurvire 1987)
research.periodic_elements.element_analy: Curium-244 alpha particles and X-rays read every element in a rock: the APXS of the Mars rovers (Sojourner 1997)
Retort oil shale in an alembic and distil the crude oil into naphtha, kerosene, diesel and bitumen (Young 1851, Drake 1859); bitumen binds asphalt roads
research.periodic_elements.diesel_engine: Diesel's compression-ignition engine turns a generator: current from oil with no boiler or water
research.periodic_elements.thermal_crack: Burton's pressure stills crack heavy oil into gasoline; the cracked gas is rich in ethylene
research.periodic_elements.coal_liquefac: Bergius hydrogenated powdered coal at 200 atmospheres into petrol and middle oil (Nobel Prize 1931)
research.periodic_elements.rocketry.desc: Goddard flew a rocket on liquid fuel and liquid oxygen (1926): kerosene rockets push an elytra like three charges of gunpowder
research.periodic_elements.pvc.desc: Vinyl chloride from ethylene and chlorine, polymerised and made flexible by Semon (1926); PVC-sleeved cable carries current four times as far as bare wire
ICI found that ethylene at 1500 atmospheres with a trace of oxygen becomes a waxy white solid (1933): first radar cable, then everything
research.periodic_elements.catalytic_ref: Platforming: naphtha over platinum becomes high-octane gasoline, benzene and xylene, and gives up hydrogen (UOP 1949)
research.periodic_elements.nylon.desc: Carothers' nylon 6-6 (DuPont 1935), the first fully synthetic fibre: stockings, rope and parachutes
research.periodic_elements.isotope_enric: The Y-12 calutrons enriched the uranium of the first bomb; afterwards they enriched lithium-6, boron-10 and hundreds of other isotopes for science
research.periodic_elements.heavy_water.d: Norsk Hydro's heavy water slows neutrons without catching them, so natural uranium can sustain a chain reaction (the Canadian CANDU reactors)
Boron-10 swallows neutrons: control rods throttle a reactor so it stops burning fuel it has no room to store
research.periodic_elements.tritium.desc: Lithium-6 in a reactor catches a neutron and splits into helium and tritium; tritium's soft beta light makes signs glow for decades with no power
research.periodic_elements.gas_compressi: Seamless drawn steel cylinders hold gas at 150 atmospheres (Mannesmann 1885): a Compressor upgrade lets a machine fill them, nine flasks to a cylinder
research.periodic_elements.regenerative_: Siemens passes the hot flue gas through brick checkerwork that then heats the incoming air: a Regenerator upgrade halves a fuel-fired machine's heat loss
research.periodic_elements.basic_refract: Thomas and Gilchrist line the converter with burnt lime and dolomite that stand the heat and the slag: a Refractory Lining lets a fuel-fired machine run 150 °C hotter
research.periodic_elements.by_product_re: By-product coke ovens catch the gas instead of burning it off: a Gas Recovery Hood bottles the gases a machine vents
research.periodic_elements.electric_moto: Tesla's induction motor turns a paddle in the vessel: a Mechanical Stirrer makes a machine work 50% faster for a quarter more fuel or current
research.periodic_elements.catalysis.des: Mittasch tests thousands of catalysts for Haber's ammonia: a Catalyst Bed doubles the rate of reactions over iron, nickel, platinum or vanadium oxide
research.periodic_elements.automatic_mil: Oliver Evans' mill moves grain from step to step with no hand on it: an Output Pusher moves a machine's products into the chest next to it
research.periodic_elements.gas_mains.des: Winsor and Clegg lit London with coal gas sent through iron mains from gasholders (1812): Fluid Pipes join machines to tanks, and Tank Plates build a tank as big as you like
research.periodic_elements.rendering.des: Simmer meat, fat and bone in a kettle: tallow for candles and soap, and protein meal for the animals
Squeeze seeds in a screw press for oil; the cake left over feeds cattle
Boil fat or oil with the potash of wood ash: soft soap, and glycerol in the liquor
research.periodic_elements.pit_tanning.d: Lay hides in pits of bark liquor for months: four pieces of flesh make one leather, slowly and without a crafting grid
research.periodic_elements.mashing.desc: Malt turns the starch of grain and potatoes into sugar, and yeast the sugar into alcohol
research.periodic_elements.sweet_oil_of_: Distil spirit with a little oil of vitriol: diethyl ether, a solvent and a fuel (Cordus)
research.periodic_elements.alum_making.d: Dissolve clay in oil of vitriol and add potash: alum crystals, which taw rabbit hide into leather (Marggraf)
research.periodic_elements.hard_soap.des: Soda ash or a handful of salt makes soap that sets in hard bars (Aleppo, Castile)
research.periodic_elements.gas_liquor.de: Wash the ammonia out of coke-oven gas and neutralise it with acid: sulfate of ammonia for the fields
research.periodic_elements.superphosphat: Dissolve bones or phosphate rock in sulfuric acid: the first factory fertilizer (Lawes)
Boil starch with a little acid and it becomes sugar, faster than malt (Kirchhoff)
research.periodic_elements.vulcanization: Tap latex from rubber trees in the jungle and cure the rubber with sulfur: tough, springy and waterproof (Goodyear)
research.periodic_elements.prussian_blue: Blood calcined with potash and struck with green vitriol: the first synthetic pigment, made in a Dye Vat (Diesbach)
research.periodic_elements.tar_distillat: Catch the tar of the coke oven and cut it in a still: benzene, carbolic acid, anthracene, and pitch for tarmac (Mansfield)
Benzene stirred into nitric and sulfuric acid: oil of mirbane, the way to aniline (Mitscherlich)
research.periodic_elements.aniline.desc: Reduce nitrobenzene with iron filings and a little acid: aniline, the base of the coal tar dyes (Bechamp)
research.periodic_elements.fuchsine.desc: Aniline and arsenic acid give magenta, the dye that made the aniline fortunes (Verguin)
research.periodic_elements.picric_acid.d: Nitrate carbolic acid three times: a yellow silk dye, and later Lyddite
research.periodic_elements.alizarin.desc: Madder red from anthracene in a pressure vessel: the end of the madder fields (Graebe, Liebermann, Caro)
research.periodic_elements.antiseptic_su: Carbolic acid on wounds, hands and instruments: carbolic soap cures an early Infection (Lister)
research.periodic_elements.anaesthesia.d: Ether on a cloth puts a patient to sleep: a cure for a zombie villager takes half as long (Morton)
research.periodic_elements.dynamite.desc: Nitroglycerin soaked into diatomite is safe to handle: Mining Charges break a 5 by 5 by 5 block of rock and keep every block (Nobel)
research.periodic_elements.cordite.desc: Nitroglycerin and guncotton in cords: Cordite Cartridges hit 25% harder from the Breech-Loading Rifle and make no smoke (Abel and Dewar)
research.periodic_elements.aspirin.desc: Salicylic acid from phenol in the Autoclave, then acetylated: aspirin eases nausea and fatigue and cures an early Infection (Kolbe, Hoffmann)
research.periodic_elements.bordeaux_mixt: Copper vitriol and lime sprayed on vines stops mildew: sprayed crops never wash out or wilt in the dark, and berry bushes stop scratching (Millardet)
research.periodic_elements.insect_powder: Dried Dalmatian daisies ground to powder: an Insect Spray that kills spiders, silverfish and endermites (and bees)
research.periodic_elements.vacuum_distil: A pump on a still lowers the boiling points: a Vacuum Pump makes a still, kettle or crystallizer work 100 °C cooler
research.periodic_elements.calcium_carbi: Quicklime and coke fused in the arc make carbide; water on carbide gives acetylene, the flame of the miner's Carbide Lamp (Willson 1892)
research.periodic_elements.calcium_cyana: Hot carbide takes up nitrogen: calcium cyanamide, the first fertilizer made from the air (Frank and Caro 1898)
research.periodic_elements.oxy_acetylene: Acetylene burnt in pure oxygen is hot enough to melt steel: a Welding Torch mends metal tools and armour with ingots and no experience (Fouche and Picard 1903)
Wood spirit and air over red-hot silver give formaldehyde, the other half of the first plastics (Hofmann 1867; made by the tonne from 1889)
research.periodic_elements.bakelite.desc: Phenol and formaldehyde under pressure set into Bakelite: hard, dark, and it takes a polish; coloured Bakelite blocks and Bakelite-cased Geiger counters (Baekeland 1907)
research.periodic_elements.urea.desc: Ammonia and carbon dioxide at 150 atmospheres become urea, the richest nitrogen fertilizer (Bosch and Meiser 1922)
research.periodic_elements.prilled_ferti: Melt dropped down a tall tower freezes into hard round prills that flow and keep: ammonium nitrate, and NPK prills that make crops grow twice as fast
research.periodic_elements.tnt.desc: Toluene nitrated three times: TNT is safe to melt and pour, and a Demolition Charge breaks even obsidian (Wilbrand 1863; army filling from 1902)
research.periodic_elements.acetone_ferme: Weizmann's bacterium turns the starch of grain or potatoes into acetone and butanol: the acetone for wartime cordite (1916)
research.periodic_elements.neoprene.desc: Chloroprene rubber from acetylene: it shrugs off oil and cold; a neoprene Wetsuit swims like a dolphin and never freezes (Carothers 1931)
research.periodic_elements.buna_rubber.d: Synthetic rubber from alcohol and benzene, no jungle needed: Rubber Wheels, and a Conveyor Belt that empties a machine four items at a time (Lebedev 1926, IG Farben 1929)
research.periodic_elements.sulfa_drugs.d: A red dye cured streptococcus in mice; its active half, sulfanilamide, cures Infection and even sepsis (Domagk 1932, Trefouel 1935)
research.periodic_elements.biodiesel.des: Plant oil or tallow with methanol and lye gives methyl esters that run a Diesel Generator: fuel from the farm (Chavanne 1937)
research.periodic_elements.polystyrene.d: Styrene joins into clear, light polystyrene; blown with gas it is foam: Foam Lagging for cool machines and Insulation that keeps ice from melting (Dow 1941)
research.periodic_elements.penicillin.de: Fleming's mould grown in deep, stirred tanks of sterile air: penicillin cures Infection, guards against it for 20 minutes, and with Weakness cures a zombie villager (1928, 1943)
An antibiotic from a soil bacterium, the first to cure tuberculosis: it cures Infection and guards against it for 20 minutes (Schatz and Waksman 1943)
research.periodic_elements.ddt.desc: An insecticide that lasts: a DDT Duster leaves ground that kills insects for three days, and the chickens near it lay half as often (Muller 1939; Silent Spring 1962)
research.periodic_elements.two_four_d.de: A plant hormone that kills broad-leaved weeds and spares grass and grain: Weed Killer clears flowers, ferns, vines and leaves (1945)
research.periodic_elements.atrazine.desc: Sprayed before anything grows: Pre-Emergent stops grass and mycelium spreading onto the ground for ten days (Geigy 1958)
research.periodic_elements.plastic_explo: RDX from hexamine, kneaded with oil: a Shaped Charge with a copper liner bores a tunnel sixteen blocks deep (Henning 1898; Munroe effect)
research.periodic_elements.anfo.desc: Fertilizer prills soaked in diesel: the cheapest blasting agent; an ANFO Charge breaks a 9x9x9 cube for the quarry (1955)
research.periodic_elements.radiation_cou: Potassium iodide tablets keep radioiodine out of the body, and Prussian blue capsules bind radiocaesium: each cuts the dose from fission products for a day
research.periodic_elements.glyphosate.de: A weed killer that kills every green plant: Field Clear spares only crops grown from tolerant seeds (Franz 1970)
research.periodic_elements.recombinant_d: Genes cut and pasted into bacteria: the Bioreactor, a chip-run vessel for engineered microbes (Cohen and Boyer 1973)
research.periodic_elements.cellulosic_et: Enzymes break the cellulose of any plant to sugar: ethanol from logs, leaves and straw
research.periodic_elements.tolerant_seed: A bacterial gene makes wheat shrug off glyphosate: Tolerant Seeds survive Field Clear and grow a tenth faster
research.periodic_elements.pla.desc: Plastic fermented from sugar that composts away: flower pots and item frames from PLA
Messenger RNA in a droplet of fat teaches the body its enemy: seven game days with no Infection (Kariko and Weissman; 2020)
research.periodic_elements.amifostine.de: A radioprotector from the Walter Reed programme: for an hour, radiation does half the harm (1959; approved 1995)
Quarrymen's sledges and navvies' broad shovels: a Sledgehammer breaks 3x3 of stone and an Excavator 3x3 of earth, slowly, at one wear per block
research.periodic_elements.rock_blasting: Black powder packed into a drilled hole (Schemnitz 1627): a Blasting Charge breaks a 3x3x3 block of stone, drops all of it and never harms a machine
research.periodic_elements.rock_drill.de: Compressed air drove the drills that cut the Mont Cenis tunnel (Sommeiller 1861; Ingersoll 1871): the Air Compressor fills cylinders and the Pneumatic Rock Drill mines one block, a 1x3 tunnel or 3x3
Plante's lead plates in sulfuric acid store charge you can carry: a Lead-Acid Battery Pack holds 1,500 kJ and fills on a Charging Bench joined to the wire
research.periodic_elements.rotary_hammer: An electric motor turns and hammers the bit at once (Bosch 1932): the Rotary Hammer runs on a battery pack and never slows you
research.periodic_elements.chainsaw.desc: A cutting chain driven round a bar (Stihl 1926): the Chainsaw fells a whole tree, up to 128 logs, on battery power
research.periodic_elements.heavy_drill.d: Diamond core drilling: the Heavy Mining Drill adds a 5x5 head and a vein mode that follows one ore up to 32 blocks
research.periodic_elements.li_ion_pack.d: Four times the charge of lead at half the weight: a Lithium-Ion Pack holds 6,000 kJ and the Heavy Mining Drill no longer slows you
research.periodic_elements.ore_seeking.d: The element analyzer built into the drill head: in vein mode, use the Heavy Mining Drill on an ore to read the whole vein before you dig
research.periodic_elements.surveying.des: Pace out the land and draw it on a tablet, as at Ga-Sur: the Field Atlas sketches what you walk past, with no coordinates
research.periodic_elements.magnetic_comp: A magnetised needle points north: the Atlas shows north, your exact place and facing, and a compass bar while you hold it
research.periodic_elements.astrolabe.des: Measure the height of the pole star and you know how far north you are: the Atlas shows Z, a scale bar, and draws twice as far
research.periodic_elements.portolan.desc: Sailors copied each other's coastlines: sneak and use the Atlas with paper in your other hand to make an Atlas Copy for someone else
research.periodic_elements.chronometer.d: Harrison's H4 keeps time at sea, and the time difference gives longitude: the Atlas shows X as well
research.periodic_elements.hot_air_ballo: The Montgolfiers' balloon lifts an observer above the land: a Survey Balloon draws 128 blocks all round at once
research.periodic_elements.triangulation: Ramsden's great theodolite measures angles to a fraction of a second: the Atlas draws sharp, with relief shading and contour lines every 8 blocks
research.periodic_elements.geological_ma: William Smith coloured England by the rock beneath the soil: the Atlas gains a layer showing the bedrock under every column you walk past
research.periodic_elements.species_plant: Linnaeus counted stamens with a hand lens and gave every plant two Latin names: the Tree Compendium shows each tree's scientific name, family and native range
research.periodic_elements.plant_geograp: Humboldt carried a barometer and thermometer up Chimborazo and saw the forests change with height and heat: the Compendium shows each biome's climate
research.periodic_elements.red_list.desc: The IUCN begins listing species at risk of extinction: the Compendium shows how threatened each tree is in the wild
research.periodic_elements.core_drilling: Leschot's drill with a crown of diamonds brings up a whole core of rock: the Atlas gains an ore layer from your cores and the ores you mine
research.periodic_elements.radiation_map: The Curies hunted uranium minerals with an electroscope: every reading you take is marked on the Atlas's radiation layer
research.periodic_elements.magnetic_pros: Magnetometers and the first seismic reflection surveys see ore bodies from the surface: an anomaly layer, without naming the ore
research.periodic_elements.geiger_survey: Carry a Geiger counter and the radiation where you walk is logged on the Atlas by itself
research.periodic_elements.radio_directi: Radio beacons let ships and aircraft fix their place: a Radio Transmitter shares your Atlas markers with every player who knows radio within 512 blocks
research.periodic_elements.radar.desc: Radio echoes off aircraft won the Battle of Britain: a Radar Station shows creatures and players within 96 blocks on the Atlas, and a Handheld Radar gives you a minimap
research.periodic_elements.gamma_spectro: A sodium iodide crystal tells the gamma rays of uranium, thorium and caesium apart: the Atlas splits radiation by isotope, and reads the ground from the air
research.periodic_elements.satellite.des: Sputnik's beeps were heard all round the world: launch a satellite and a Tracking Station maps 512 blocks all round it each day, without going there
research.periodic_elements.landsat.desc: Landsat saw rocks and minerals in bands of light the eye cannot: your satellites note the rock and the ores near the surface of what they map
research.periodic_elements.gps.desc: Atomic clocks in orbit give anyone their place to a few metres: a GPS Receiver shows the minimap anywhere, marks where you die and routes you to your markers
research.periodic_elements.de_re_metalli: Agricola describes every ore and how miners find it: the Mineral Compendium shows each ore's mineral and the depths where it is found
research.periodic_elements.theory_of_the: Hutton reads at Siccar Point that rocks are made, worn away and made again: the Compendium sorts rocks into igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic and names the formation underfoot
research.periodic_elements.thin_sections: Sorby grinds rock to slices thin enough to see through under a microscope: the Compendium shows the minerals each rock is made of
research.periodic_elements.xray_diffract: The Braggs bounce X-rays off crystals and read the spacing of their atoms: the Compendium shows each mineral's formula and crystal system
research.periodic_elements.heated_greenh: Glass houses warmed by a stove (Chelsea Physic Garden 1681): tropical and desert plants grow far from home
research.periodic_elements.cold_greenhou: Linde's refrigerating machine (1876) keeps a glasshouse cold: arctic and alpine plants grow anywhere; ice will do while it lasts
research.periodic_elements.alkaloids.des: Pelletier and Caventou drew emetine and quinine out of plants with acid water; Runge found caffeine (1819)
research.periodic_elements.food_antioxid: Fat kept from going rancid with a pinch of NDGA from the creosote bush (1943), until safer antioxidants replaced it
research.periodic_elements.vitamins.desc: Szent-Györgyi drew hexuronic acid out of paprika (1928): vitamin C, the cure for scurvy, and with the same methods arbutin from bearberry
research.periodic_elements.domestication: Keep the seeds of the best plants: the Seed Lens shows what traits a seed or a crop has
research.periodic_elements.animal_husban: Pen the herd and feed it: a Feeding Trough feeds the animals around it so they breed and grow
research.periodic_elements.crop_rotation: Three-field rotation: soybeans, beans, indigo and alfalfa leave the ground fertilized when harvested
Blue from indigo, red from madder root: the Dye Vat dyes with plants
research.periodic_elements.plant_hybridi: Kölreuter crossed tobacco plants by hand: the Pollination Brush chooses the father of a plant's seeds
Tobacco steeped in water kills caterpillars on crops: the first insecticide of the farm
Mendel counted his peas: each trait is two factors, one from each parent. The Seed Lens shows the genes themselves
research.periodic_elements.silage.desc: Goffart packed green maize in a pit and it kept all winter: the Silo turns maize, sorghum and alfalfa into silage
research.periodic_elements.nitrogen_fixa: Hellriegel and Wilfarth show that bacteria in the root nodules of legumes take nitrogen from the air: Inoculant gives a legume its rhizobia
Shull and Jones cross inbred lines of maize: the first generation grows with hybrid vigour. The Seed Lens marks hybrids and pure lines
research.periodic_elements.balanced_feed: Feed with energy, protein, minerals and salt in the right shares: animals grow and breed faster on it
research.periodic_elements.x_ray_mutagen: Stadler X-rays barley seeds and the plants come out changed: the Seed Irradiator makes mutations twenty times as common
research.periodic_elements.dna_double_he: Franklin's X-ray picture, Watson and Crick's model: genes are written in DNA. The Seed Lens shows every trait, and the stature gene of wheat and rice
A cobalt-60 source in a field of crops (Japan 1960): seeds of the plants around it mutate twenty times as often
research.periodic_elements.dna_sequencin: Sanger reads DNA letter by letter: the DNA Sequencer shows the whole genome of a seed
research.periodic_elements.pcr.desc: Mullis copies a stretch of DNA a billion times by heating and cooling it: the Thermocycler tests seeds for a marker's genes and sorts them
Sanford shoots gold beads coated with DNA into plant cells: the Gene Gun gives crops the Bt, EPSPS, golden rice and DREB genes
research.periodic_elements.crispr.desc: Charpentier and Doudna turn a bacterial defence into scissors for DNA: the CRISPR Kit rewrites one gene of a crop
research.periodic_elements.belt_conveyor: Thomas Robins' rubber-covered belt carries coal and ore for miles (1891): the faster Rubber Belt, the Steel Hopper to keep up with it, and the Belt Sorter that turns chosen items aside
research.periodic_elements.assembly_line: Ford's line brings the work to the worker on rollers and chains (1913): the Roller Conveyor and the Stainless Steel Hopper
research.periodic_elements.hide_tent.des: Hides on a frame of poles: a Tent you sleep in far from home, which never moves your spawn point
A leather bag on two straps: a Leather Backpack with 27 places that picks up the plant and mineral specimens you walk over
A knotted net thrown over game: the Rope Net catches a small animal alive and lets it out where you throw it
research.periodic_elements.explorer_comp: Bearings and travellers' accounts: choose a biome and the Explorer's Compass points to the nearest one
research.periodic_elements.animal_cage.d: The menageries' travelling cages: the Steel Cage carries any animal, a horse or a cow too, and never wears out
research.periodic_elements.electric_cap_: Edison's miner's lamp: a tungsten bulb on the helmet fed by the battery pack, light 15 that follows you
research.periodic_elements.sodium_lighti: Low-pressure sodium vapour shines yellow at 589 nm: a Sodium Lamp on a post keeps monsters from spawning within 24 blocks
A silver-oxygen-caesium photocathode turns faint infrared into a picture: Night Vision Goggles show the dark and outline monsters
research.periodic_elements.nylon_pack.de: Light, tough nylon on an aluminium frame: a Nylon Backpack with 54 places
Blue gallium nitride light (Nakamura 1993) under a yellow phosphor gives white: LED Lamps reach 40 blocks on little power, and the LED Spotlight Helmet lights where you look
research.periodic_elements.sericulture.d: Silkworms fed on white mulberry leaves spin cocoons; boiled, each gives one long silk thread (Leizu, China)
research.periodic_elements.carmine.desc: The Aztecs' crimson of dried cochineal, shipped to Europe by Spain: dye red in a Dye Vat with cochineal
research.periodic_elements.shellac.desc: Sticklac scraped from Indian trees, washed and melted: shellac, varnish for furniture and the insulation of early electricity
research.periodic_elements.origin_of_spe: Darwin's finches and pigeons: species change by natural selection. The Animal Compendium tells each animal's story
research.periodic_elements.antivenom.des: Calmette raises horse serum against snake venom: venom, salt and a bottle make Antivenom, which cures poison
research.periodic_elements.hirudin.desc: The anticoagulant of the medicinal leech, drawn out in a Digestion Vat
research.periodic_elements.exenatide.des: A peptide from Gila monster saliva becomes a diabetes medicine, made in the Bioreactor
research.periodic_elements.guano.desc: Peruvian seabird guano, leached with hot water and potash: saltpetre for powder and fields (the Guano Age, 1840-1880)
research.periodic_elements.galalith.desc: Casein from skim milk hardened in formalin: galalith, the milk-stone of buttons and pens (Spitteler and Krische 1897)
research.periodic_elements.tyrian_purple: The Phoenicians' purple from murex snails, worth more than gold: dye purple in a Dye Vat with murex
research.periodic_elements.vitamin_d.des: Cod and shark liver oil cures rickets (McCollum 1922): vitamin D3 drawn out in a Digestion Vat
research.periodic_elements.chitosan.desc: Crab shells boiled in strong lye lose their acetyl groups: chitosan, for wound dressings and water filters (Rouget 1859)
research.periodic_elements.lal_test.desc: Horseshoe crab blood clots at a trace of bacterial endotoxin: every injectable medicine is tested with it (Bang and Levin)
research.periodic_elements.gfp.desc: The glow of the crystal jelly made by bacteria: GFP, a living marker for cells (Shimomura 1962, Chalfie 1994)
block.periodic_elements.charcoal_pit.des: An earth-covered wood pile that smoulders with little air
block.periodic_elements.lime_kiln.desc: A stone shaft kiln that burns limestone into quicklime
block.periodic_elements.smelting_furnace: A clay furnace that roasts copper ore and reduces it with charcoal
block.periodic_elements.bloomery.desc: A charcoal shaft furnace that reduces iron ore to a spongy bloom
block.periodic_elements.crucible.desc: A clay crucible set in the fire to melt and mix metals
block.periodic_elements.cupel.desc: A bone-ash dish that soaks up molten litharge and leaves silver
block.periodic_elements.alembic.desc: A still with a glass head that boils and condenses what it distils
block.periodic_elements.crystallizer.des: Leaching vats and a boiling pan for crystallizing salts
block.periodic_elements.charcoal_blast_f: A tall charcoal furnace that melts iron into pig iron
block.periodic_elements.cementation_furn: Sealed chests of iron bars and charcoal held red-hot for days
block.periodic_elements.zinc_retort.desc: A closed clay retort that reduces zinc ore and condenses the metal
block.periodic_elements.amalgamation_pan: A pan to work ore with mercury and a hood to drive the mercury off
block.periodic_elements.phosphorus_retor: A clay retort heated white-hot whose neck dips under water
block.periodic_elements.reverberatory_fu: A furnace whose roof throws the flame down onto the ore; the flue catches fumes
block.periodic_elements.pottery_kiln.des: An updraft kiln that fires clay into brick and terracotta
block.periodic_elements.salt_pan.desc: Shallow clay pans where sun and wind dry seawater to salt
block.periodic_elements.desalination_sti: A copper pot still over a fire: seawater boils and its steam condenses as pure fresh water; the salt stays in the pot
block.periodic_elements.fermentation_bar: A sealed oak barrel where yeast turns sugar into alcohol
block.periodic_elements.vinegar_vat.desc: An open vat where wine sours into vinegar in the air
block.periodic_elements.glass_furnace.de: A beehive furnace whose clay pots melt sand with wood ash
block.periodic_elements.porcelain_kiln.d: A climbing kiln whose last chamber reaches 1300 °C
block.periodic_elements.coke_oven.desc: A brick beehive oven that bakes coal for two days into coke
block.periodic_elements.huntsman_furnace: Clay crucibles of steel melted in a coke fire with a tall chimney
block.periodic_elements.pneumatic_trough: A retort over a water trough that collects the gas it gives off
block.periodic_elements.electrolysis_cel: Electrodes in a molten salt; powered by Voltaic Piles next to it
block.periodic_elements.digestion_vat.de: A porcelain-lined vat where hot acid dissolves ores
block.periodic_elements.reduction_crucib: A sealed iron crucible where potassium strips oxygen and chlorine from salts
block.periodic_elements.lead_chamber.des: A room of lead sheet where burning sulfur becomes sulfuric acid
block.periodic_elements.bessemer_convert: A tilting steel pear lined with firebrick: air blown through molten iron burns out its carbon
block.periodic_elements.bayer_digester.d: A steel pressure vessel where hot lye dissolves the alumina out of bauxite
block.periodic_elements.hall_heroult_cel: A carbon-lined steel pot of molten cryolite; current splits the alumina dissolved in it
block.periodic_elements.chlor_alkali_cel: A slate box with a flowing mercury cathode: brine becomes lye and chlorine
block.periodic_elements.solvay_tower.des: A tall cast-iron tower where ammoniated brine meets carbon dioxide
block.periodic_elements.contact_converte: Trays of vanadium catalyst that turn sulfur dioxide into sulfur trioxide
block.periodic_elements.air_liquefier.de: A compressor and copper heat exchanger that liquefy air and boil it apart by temperature
block.periodic_elements.spectroscope_ben: A prism spectroscope with a Bunsen burner: names the traces in a residue so they can be separated
block.periodic_elements.electrolytic_ref: Lead-lined tanks where current carries copper from crude anodes to pure cathodes
block.periodic_elements.mond_reactor.des: Towers where carbon monoxide carries nickel off as a gas and lays it down pure
block.periodic_elements.moissan_cell.des: A platinum U-tube with fluorite stoppers for electrolysing hydrogen fluoride
block.periodic_elements.electric_arc_fur: Three graphite electrodes strike an arc into the charge: ferroalloys and silicon at 2000 °C and more
block.periodic_elements.high_pressure_re: A thick steel bomb where nitrogen and hydrogen meet over an iron catalyst at 200 atmospheres
block.periodic_elements.ostwald_converte: Ammonia and air flash over a red-hot platinum-rhodium gauze and become nitric acid
block.periodic_elements.flotation_cell.d: Stirred tanks where oily bubbles carry sulfide grains up as froth and the rock sinks
block.periodic_elements.sintering_furnac: A hydrogen furnace where pressed tungsten carbide and cobalt powder bake into solid tips
block.periodic_elements.fractional_cryst: Rows of dishes for crystallizing salts again and again, with a muffle to ignite them to oxides
block.periodic_elements.van_arkel_reacto: A glass bulb where a glowing tungsten wire grows a bar of pure metal from its iodide vapour
block.periodic_elements.chlorinator.desc: A brick-lined shaft where chlorine meets hot ore and coke; titanium tetrachloride boils off
block.periodic_elements.kroll_reactor.de: A stainless steel retort under argon where molten magnesium strips the chlorine from titanium
block.periodic_elements.ion_exchange_col: Tall glass columns of resin beads: each rare earth comes off in its own band
block.periodic_elements.crystal_puller.d: A quartz crucible of molten silicon under argon; a turning seed draws up one crystal
block.periodic_elements.zone_refiner.des: A boat of germanium drawn slowly through ring heaters: the impurities ride the molten zone
block.periodic_elements.diamond_press.de: A belt press of cemented carbide anvils: 50000 atmospheres and 1500 °C
block.periodic_elements.enrichment_casca: Thousands of porous nickel barriers in a row: uranium hexafluoride gas comes out a little richer in uranium-235 at each
block.periodic_elements.hot_cell.desc: Lead walls and a metre of lead glass: remote hands dissolve spent fuel in nitric acid and part it by solvent
block.periodic_elements.cyclotron.desc: Two hollow copper electrodes between the poles of a great magnet whirl alpha particles into a target
block.periodic_elements.calutron.desc: A vacuum tank between the poles of a great magnet: ions of each isotope bend into their own collector pocket
block.periodic_elements.chip_fab.desc: A clean room of diffusion furnaces, photomask steppers and etching baths that builds circuits layer by layer on silicon
block.periodic_elements.heavy_ion_accele: A linear accelerator and superconducting separator: heavy ions slam into a spinning target and the rare survivors are caught in a detector
block.periodic_elements.refinery_still.d: A riveted steel still under a fractionating column: oil boils off cut by cut, light to heavy
block.periodic_elements.cracking_unit.de: A pressure still over a furnace that breaks heavy oil into gasoline and gas; later a platinum reformer
block.periodic_elements.soap_kettle.desc: A copper kettle over a brick hearth for rendering fat and boiling soap
block.periodic_elements.oil_press.desc: A wooden screw press that squeezes oil out of seeds
block.periodic_elements.tanning_pit.desc: A pit of bark liquor where hides lie for months to become leather
block.periodic_elements.vulcanizer.desc: An iron steam pan that cures rubber with sulfur under pressure
block.periodic_elements.dye_vat.desc: A copper-lined vat over a small fire where pigments are precipitated and dyes made
block.periodic_elements.tar_still.desc: An iron pot still with a column that cuts coal tar into its oils and leaves pitch
block.periodic_elements.autoclave.desc: A bolted steel pressure vessel for reactions at 200 °C and 20 atmospheres
block.periodic_elements.prilling_tower.d: An electric melt pot at the top of a tall tower: drops of fertilizer freeze into prills as they fall
block.periodic_elements.deep_tank_fermen: A steel tank stirred and blown with sterile air: the only way to grow antibiotics by the tonne
block.periodic_elements.bioreactor.desc: A sterile glass and steel vessel run by a chip: engineered microbes make fuels, plastics and medicines
block.periodic_elements.air_compressor.d: An electric piston compressor: draws in air and fills Steel Cylinders with it, no Compressor upgrade needed
reaction.periodic_elements.wood_drying.d: Drives off moisture as steam (2.26 kJ/g to boil plus heating)
reaction.periodic_elements.cellulose_car: Cellulose chars to carbon; tar and gases escape
reaction.periodic_elements.lignin_carbon: Lignin is richer in carbon and leaves more charcoal
reaction.periodic_elements.limestone_cal: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2 (+178 kJ/mol plus heating the stone)
reaction.periodic_elements.chalcopyrite_: CuFeS2 + 3 O2 -> CuO + FeO + 2 SO2 (gives off heat)
reaction.periodic_elements.pyrite_sulfat: FeS2 + 3 O2 -> FeSO4 + SO2: a gentle roast below 650 °C gives green vitriol
reaction.periodic_elements.pyrite_roasti: 4 FeS2 + 11 O2 -> 2 Fe2O3 + 8 SO2 (gives off heat)
reaction.periodic_elements.copper_oxide_: 2 CuO + C -> 2 Cu + CO2; above 1085 °C the copper melts and pools
reaction.periodic_elements.iron_oxide_re: 2 Fe2O3 + 3 C -> 4 Fe + 3 CO2 (+468 kJ per 2 mol plus heating)
Native gold melts at 1064 °C and runs out of the quartz
reaction.periodic_elements.cassiterite_r: SnO2 + C -> Sn + CO2; tin melts at 232 °C and runs out of the charge
reaction.periodic_elements.galena_roasti: 2 PbS + 3 O2 -> 2 PbO + 2 SO2 (gives off heat)
reaction.periodic_elements.litharge_redu: 2 PbO + C -> 2 Pb + CO2; lead melts at 327 °C
reaction.periodic_elements.cinnabar_roas: HgS + O2 -> Hg + SO2; the mercury vapour is condensed
reaction.periodic_elements.bronze_alloyi: Copper melted with a tenth of its weight of tin gives bronze
reaction.periodic_elements.cupellation.d: Lead oxidizes into the bone-ash cupel as litharge; the silver stays behind as a bead
reaction.periodic_elements.wood_distilla: Dry distillation of wood: charcoal stays, wood spirit and vinegar condense
reaction.periodic_elements.lignin_distil: Lignin leaves more charcoal and some wood spirit
reaction.periodic_elements.oil_of_vitrio: 2 FeSO4 -> Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3; the SO3 in water is oil of vitriol (put water in the reagent slot)
reaction.periodic_elements.aqua_fortis.d: KNO3 + H2SO4 -> HNO3 + KHSO4; nitric acid distils over at 83 °C
reaction.periodic_elements.saltpeter_lea: Nitre earth leached with potash; the liquor is boiled down and saltpetre crystallizes
reaction.periodic_elements.cast_iron.des: Fe2O3 reduced and carburized until the iron melts at about 1150 °C and runs out as pig iron
reaction.periodic_elements.cast_iron_mag: Fe3O4 reduced and carburized into pig iron
reaction.periodic_elements.iron_cementat: Wrought iron packed in charcoal soaks up about 1% carbon and becomes blister steel
reaction.periodic_elements.sphalerite_ro: 2 ZnS + 3 O2 -> 2 ZnO + 2 SO2 (gives off heat)
reaction.periodic_elements.zinc_oxide_re: ZnO + C -> Zn + CO; zinc boils at 907 °C, so the retort condenses its vapour
reaction.periodic_elements.brass_alloyin: Copper melted with zinc (70:30) gives brass
reaction.periodic_elements.type_metal_al: Lead with antimony and tin casts sharp, hard type
reaction.periodic_elements.phosphorus_fr: Bone ash heated white-hot with charcoal; phosphorus vapour is caught under water
reaction.periodic_elements.gold_amalgama: Mercury dissolves the gold; heating the amalgam drives the mercury off (a little is lost)
reaction.periodic_elements.silver_amalga: Mercury takes up the silver; heating the amalgam leaves the silver
reaction.periodic_elements.arsenopyrite_: 2 FeAsS + 5 O2 -> Fe2O3 + As2O3 + 2 SO2; white arsenic sublimes into the flue
reaction.periodic_elements.arsenic_reduc: As2O3 + 3 C -> 2 As + 3 CO; grey arsenic sublimes at 614 °C
reaction.periodic_elements.bismuth_liqua: Native bismuth melts at 271 °C and runs out of the ore
reaction.periodic_elements.cobaltite_roa: Roasting drives the arsenic off as white arsenic and leaves cobalt oxide (zaffre)
reaction.periodic_elements.clay_firing.d: Kaolinite loses its water at 550 °C and the clay sinters into brick with its quartz; the quartz comes with the clay
reaction.periodic_elements.brine_evapora: Sun and wind evaporate the water (2.26 kJ/g, taken from the air, so no fuel is needed)
reaction.periodic_elements.salt_crystall: Common salt crystallizes first; the bitter magnesium salts stay in the last liquor (bittern)
Seawater boiled in a still: the steam condenses as pure fresh water, like distilled water (ships' stills, Hawkins 1594)
reaction.periodic_elements.still_salt.de: Common salt scraped from the pot once the water has boiled off; the bitter salts are left as bittern
reaction.periodic_elements.sugar_ferment: C12H22O11 + H2O -> 4 C2H5OH + 4 CO2; put water in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.vinegar_souri: C2H5OH + O2 -> CH3COOH + H2O; the oxygen comes from the air
Sand melted with twice its weight of wood ash: potash is the flux and lime makes the glass hard; put wood ash in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.spirit_of_sal: NaCl + H2SO4 -> HCl + NaHSO4 (Glauber, 1648); put sulfuric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.gold_dissolut: Au + HNO3 + 4 HCl -> HAuCl4 + NO + 2 H2O, then green vitriol drops pure gold; silver stays behind as chloride; put aqua regia in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.kaolin_firing: Kaolin with extra quartz fired at 1300 °C vitrifies into hard white porcelain; put quartz or sand in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.coal_coking.d: Coal baked without air for two days: its fixed carbon stays behind as coke (Darby 1709)
reaction.periodic_elements.coal_tar_cond: Half the hydrogen of coal comes over as tar, caught in the condensers; put empty flasks in the flask slot
reaction.periodic_elements.coal_degassin: The hydrogen in coal leaves as coal gas and tar
The oxygen in coal leaves as coal gas and tar
reaction.periodic_elements.ammonia_liquo: The nitrogen in coal leaves as ammonia, washed out of the gas into ammonia water; put empty flasks in the flask slot
reaction.periodic_elements.coal_degassin: The nitrogen in coal leaves as ammonia water and tar
The sulfur in coal leaves as hydrogen sulfide and tar
reaction.periodic_elements.tungsten_stee: Steel melted with tungsten and a little manganese: Mushet's self-hardening steel (1868); put tungsten in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.crucible_stee: Blister steel melted in a closed crucible: the carbon spreads evenly and the slag floats off (Huntsman 1740); needs coke
reaction.periodic_elements.hydrogen_from: Fe + H2SO4 -> FeSO4 + H2: Cavendish's inflammable air, caught under water; put sulfuric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.nitre_decompo: 2 KNO3 -> K2O + N2 + 5/2 O2: red-hot saltpetre gives off oxygen and nitrogen (Scheele)
reaction.periodic_elements.salt_electrol: Molten NaCl -> Na + 1/2 Cl2 (703 kJ per 100 units; Davy 1807 used caustic soda)
reaction.periodic_elements.sylvite_elect: Molten KCl -> K + 1/2 Cl2 (Davy 1807 used caustic potash)
reaction.periodic_elements.water_electro: H2O -> H2 + 1/2 O2 in acidified water (Nicholson and Carlisle 1800)
reaction.periodic_elements.magnesium_ele: Molten MgCl2 from bittern -> Mg + Cl2 (Bunsen 1852)
reaction.periodic_elements.lime_electrol: Moist lime on a mercury cathode -> calcium amalgam, then the mercury is distilled off (Davy 1808)
reaction.periodic_elements.baryta_electr: Moist baryta on a mercury cathode (Davy 1808)
reaction.periodic_elements.strontia_elec: Moist strontia on a mercury cathode (Davy 1808)
reaction.periodic_elements.lithium_elect: Molten LiCl -> Li + 1/2 Cl2 (Bunsen and Matthiessen 1855)
reaction.periodic_elements.barite_reduct: BaSO4 + C -> BaO + SO2 + CO: heavy spar roasted with charcoal gives baryta
reaction.periodic_elements.celestine_red: SrSO4 + C -> SrO + SO2 + CO: celestine roasted with charcoal gives strontia
reaction.periodic_elements.borax_leachin: Borax + H2SO4 -> 4 H3BO3 + Na2SO4 + 5 H2O; boric acid crystallizes as the liquor cools; put sulfuric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.spodumene_lea: Roasted spodumene leached with hydrochloric acid gives lithium chloride; put hydrochloric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.boron_reducti: 2 H3BO3 + 6 K -> 2 B + 3 K2O + 3 H2O (Davy, Gay-Lussac and Thenard 1808); put potassium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.beryl_chlorin: Beryl heated with charcoal in chlorine gives beryllium chloride; put chlorine in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.beryllium_red: BeCl2 + 2 K -> Be + 2 KCl (Wohler 1828); put potassium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.sulfur_chambe: S + 3/2 O2 + H2O -> H2SO4, with saltpetre fumes as the go-between (Roebuck 1746); put water in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.pyrite_chambe: Burnt pyrite gives the chamber its sulfur; the red sludge left on the floor holds selenium (Berzelius 1817); put water in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.selenium_subl: Selenium boils at 685 °C and condenses in the flue
reaction.periodic_elements.bromine_liber: MgBr2 + Cl2 -> MgCl2 + Br2: chlorine frees bromine from bittern, which distils at 59 °C (Balard 1826); put chlorine in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.iodine_from_k: Kelp ash with oil of vitriol gives off violet iodine vapour (Courtois 1811); put sulfuric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.cadmium_reduc: CdO + C -> Cd + CO: cadmium boils at 767 °C, before zinc, and comes over first (Stromeyer 1817)
reaction.periodic_elements.platinum_diss: Crude platinum dissolved in aqua regia, thrown down with sal ammoniac and heated to sponge (Wollaston 1800s); put aqua regia in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.pitchblende_r: 3 UO2 + O2 -> U3O8: Klaproth took this oxide for the new metal uranium (1789)
reaction.periodic_elements.bessemer_deca: Air blown through molten pig iron burns its carbon to carbon monoxide; the heat keeps the charge molten (Bessemer 1856)
reaction.periodic_elements.manganese_ste: Blown steel recarburized with ferromanganese to 12% manganese: Hadfield's steel hardens as it is struck (1882); put manganese in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.bessemer_stee: The blown metal is cast as mild steel: tonnes in twenty minutes instead of days
reaction.periodic_elements.pyrolusite_re: MnO2 + 2 C -> Mn + 2 CO: pyrolusite smelted with coke gives ferromanganese (Mushet 1856)
reaction.periodic_elements.gibbsite_dige: Hot lye dissolves the gibbsite in bauxite; pure aluminium hydroxide crystallizes from the cooled liquor and is calcined to alumina; iron oxide stays behind as red mud (Bayer 1888); put lye in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.gallium_liquo: Gallium follows aluminium into the Bayer liquor and is drawn off as its oxide
reaction.periodic_elements.alumina_elect: 2 Al2O3 + 3 C -> 4 Al + 3 CO2: alumina dissolved in molten cryolite is split by current and the carbon anode burns (Hall and Heroult 1886); put cryolite in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.brine_electro: NaCl + H2O -> NaOH + 1/2 Cl2 + 1/2 H2: sodium dissolves in the mercury cathode and meets water in a second cell (Castner and Kellner 1892); put water in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.solvay_soda.d: 2 NaCl + CaCO3 -> Na2CO3 + CaCl2: brine saturated with ammonia takes up carbon dioxide from burnt limestone and drops sodium bicarbonate; the ammonia is recovered (Solvay 1861); put limestone or calcite in the reagent slot
Burnt sulfur passed over vanadium oxide at 450 °C becomes SO3 and is absorbed in acid: stronger and faster than the lead chamber; put water in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.nitrogen_frac: Liquid air boils apart: nitrogen first at -196 °C (Linde 1895)
reaction.periodic_elements.oxygen_fracti: Oxygen stays in the boiling liquid until -183 °C
reaction.periodic_elements.argon_fractio: Argon boils between nitrogen and oxygen; Rayleigh and Ramsay found it as the extra weight of nitrogen from air (1894)
reaction.periodic_elements.neon_fraction: Neon from the first, most volatile fraction (Ramsay and Travers 1898); boosted for play
reaction.periodic_elements.krypton_fract: Krypton from the residue of evaporated liquid air (Ramsay and Travers 1898); boosted for play
reaction.periodic_elements.xenon_fractio: Xenon, the rarest stable gas of the air (Ramsay and Travers 1898); boosted for play
reaction.periodic_elements.helium_fracti: Helium, which never liquefies in the machine, comes off with the neon (Kayser found it in air, 1895); boosted for play
reaction.periodic_elements.bench_zinc_ox: The bench separates the residue into the compounds you can name
An indigo line in the spectrum of zinc dust: indium (Reich and Richter 1863)
reaction.periodic_elements.bench_germani: Germanium oxide separated from zinc dust: Mendeleev's eka-silicon (Winkler 1886)
reaction.periodic_elements.bench_thalliu: A green line in the spectrum of chamber sludge: thallium (Crookes 1861)
reaction.periodic_elements.copper_refini: Crude copper anodes dissolve and pure copper plates out on the cathodes; silver gold selenium tellurium and the platinum metals fall to the floor as anode slime (Elkington 1869); slime boosted for play
reaction.periodic_elements.slime_telluri: Tellurium recovered from anode slime (first found in gold ore by Muller 1782)
reaction.periodic_elements.slime_platinu: Platinum thrown down from aqua regia with sal ammoniac; put aqua regia in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.slime_palladi: Palladium thrown down from the aqua regia solution as its cyanide (Wollaston 1802); put aqua regia in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.slime_rhodium: Rose-red rhodium salt crystallized from the last liquor (Wollaston 1804); put aqua regia in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.slime_rutheni: Ruthenium from the black residue that aqua regia leaves (Klaus 1844)
Osmium from the insoluble residue: its oxide smells sharply (Tennant 1803)
reaction.periodic_elements.slime_iridium: Iridium from the insoluble residue: its salts have rainbow colours (Tennant 1803)
reaction.periodic_elements.pentlandite_r: Nickel matte roasted dead: the sulfur burns off and the iron slags
reaction.periodic_elements.nickel_carbon: Reduced nickel takes up carbon monoxide at 50 °C as volatile Ni(CO)4 and lays down pure nickel at 230 °C (Mond 1890)
reaction.periodic_elements.fluorite_dige: CaF2 + H2SO4 -> 2 HF + CaSO4 (Scheele 1771); put sulfuric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.cryolite_wash: The cryolite in fluorspar is picked out and washed
reaction.periodic_elements.hf_electrolys: Hydrogen fluoride with potassium bifluoride electrolysed in platinum: yellow fluorine at the anode (Moissan 1886)
reaction.periodic_elements.wolframite_ro: Wolframite fused with soda: the tungsten goes into sodium tungstate; put soda in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.tungstate_pre: Acid throws down yellow tungstic acid, calcined to WO3; put hydrochloric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.tungsten_redu: WO3 + 3 C -> W + 3 CO: the Elhuyar brothers reduced tungstic oxide with charcoal (1783)
reaction.periodic_elements.vanadinite_ro: Vanadinite roasted with soda: the vanadium leaches out as sodium vanadate and the lead stays as litharge; put soda in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.vanadate_prec: Acid throws down red vanadium pentoxide; put sulfuric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.vanadium_ther: 3 V2O5 + 10 Al -> 6 V + 5 Al2O3: aluminium burns the oxygen out in a white-hot flash (Goldschmidt thermite 1898); put aluminium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.germanium_fum: Germanium oxide fumes off the roasting blende and settles in the flue
reaction.periodic_elements.indium_fuming: Indium oxide fumes off the roasting blende and settles in the flue
reaction.periodic_elements.germanium_red: GeO2 + 2 H2 -> Ge + 2 H2O (Winkler 1886); put hydrogen in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.thorianite_ch: Thorium oxide dissolved in hydrochloric acid and dried to the chloride; put hydrochloric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.thorium_reduc: ThCl4 + 4 K -> Th + 4 KCl (Berzelius 1829); put potassium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.rubidium_leac: The rubidium in lepidolite leaches out with the lithium; put hydrochloric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.caesium_leach: The caesium in pollucite leaches out with the lithium; put hydrochloric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.rubidium_elec: Molten RbCl electrolysed: Bunsen named rubidium for its two red lines (1861)
reaction.periodic_elements.caesium_elect: Molten caesium chloride electrolysed (Setterberg 1882); Bunsen and Kirchhoff named caesium for its sky-blue lines (1860)
reaction.periodic_elements.gallium_elect: Gallium plated from alkaline solution (Lecoq de Boisbaudran 1875); it melts in the hand
reaction.periodic_elements.indium_electr: Indium plated from its dissolved oxide
reaction.periodic_elements.radium_electr: Radium chloride electrolysed onto mercury and the mercury boiled off (Curie and Debierne 1910)
reaction.periodic_elements.helium_releas: Hot pitchblende gives off the helium its uranium made over aeons; the spectroscope showed the sun's yellow line (Ramsay 1895)
reaction.periodic_elements.residue_radiu: Radium stays with the barium in the roasted residue
reaction.periodic_elements.residue_polon: Polonium stays with the bismuth in the roasted residue
reaction.periodic_elements.residue_actin: Actinium stays with the rare earths in the roasted residue
reaction.periodic_elements.radium_conver: Radium-barium sulfate boiled with soda and dissolved in acid; radium chloride crystallizes first over thousands of steps (Marie Curie 1902); put hydrochloric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.polonium_sepa: Polonium follows bismuth and is separated by its activity (Marie and Pierre Curie 1898)
reaction.periodic_elements.radon_collect: Radium salt gives off radon gas, pumped off and sealed in gold tubes as therapy seeds (Dorn 1900); put gold in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.cellulose_nit: Cellulose in cold nitric and sulfuric acid becomes guncotton, gelled with ether into smokeless powder (Vieille 1884); put nitric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.silica_reduct: SiO2 + 2 C -> Si + 2 CO: quartz reduced by coke in the arc (Moissan 1890s; Acheson); put coke in the fuel slot
reaction.periodic_elements.chromite_smel: FeCr2O4 + 4 C -> Fe + 2 Cr + 4 CO: chromite smelted with coke into ferrochrome (Moissan 1893)
reaction.periodic_elements.stainless_ste: Iron melted with chromium to 12.8%: Brearley's rustless steel (1913); put ferrochrome or chromium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.high_speed_st: Tungsten steel melted with molybdenum and hardened from near melting (Taylor and White 1900); load tungsten steel ingots and put molybdenum in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.tantalum_redu: Ta2O5 + 5 C -> 2 Ta + 5 CO, melted to ductile metal in the arc (von Bolton 1903)
reaction.periodic_elements.niobium_reduc: Nb2O5 + 5 C -> 2 Nb + 5 CO in the arc
reaction.periodic_elements.chromite_roas: Chromite roasted in air with soda: yellow sodium chromate leaches out and iron oxide stays (Vauquelin's route); put soda ash in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.chromate_redu: Sodium chromate fired with sulfur gives chrome green oxide; put sulfur in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.chromium_ther: Cr2O3 + 2 Al -> 2 Cr + Al2O3: carbon-free chromium in a thermite flash (Goldschmidt 1898); put aluminium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.ammonia_synth: N2 + 3 H2 -> 2 NH3 over an iron catalyst at 200 atm (Haber 1909, Bosch 1913); put hydrogen in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.ammonia_oxida: NH3 + 2 O2 -> HNO3 + H2O: ammonia burned in air on a platinum gauze, the gas absorbed in water (Ostwald 1902)
reaction.periodic_elements.molybdenite_f: Oily bubbles lift the molybdenite flakes out of the crushed rock as froth (froth flotation 1905)
reaction.periodic_elements.rhenium_flota: The rhenium sulfide floats with the molybdenite
reaction.periodic_elements.molybdenite_r: 2 MoS2 + 7 O2 -> 2 MoO3 + 4 SO2: molybdenite roasted in air (Hjelm 1781)
reaction.periodic_elements.molybdenum_re: MoO3 + 3 H2 -> Mo + 3 H2O: grey molybdenum powder; put hydrogen in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.rhenium_roast: Rhenium heptoxide boils away from the roasting molybdenite and settles in the flue (Noddack, Tacke and Berg 1925)
reaction.periodic_elements.rhenium_reduc: Re2O7 + 7 H2 -> 2 Re + 7 H2O; put hydrogen in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.carbide_sinte: W + C -> WC, pressed with 10% cobalt and sintered: Widia, hard as diamond (Krupp 1926); coke in the fuel slot, cobalt in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.beryllium_cop: Copper with 2% beryllium: as hard as steel and it never strikes a spark (1920s); put beryllium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.tantalite_dig: Coltan dissolved in hydrofluoric acid; tantalum crystallizes first as its potassium fluoride salt and is calcined (Marignac 1866); put hydrogen fluoride in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.columbite_dig: Niobium stays in the mother liquor after the tantalum salt crystallizes (Marignac 1866); put hydrogen fluoride in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.zircon_fusion: Zircon fused with lye: water glass washes out and zirconia stays, with the hafnium nobody yet knew was there; put lye in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.zirconia_redu: ZrO2 + 2 Ca -> Zr + 2 CaO: brittle zirconium powder; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.zirconium_cry: Zirconium iodide vapour splits on a glowing tungsten wire and grows a bar of ductile metal; the iodine goes round again (van Arkel and de Boer 1925); put iodine in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.hafnium_separ: Hafnium recrystallized away from zirconium as its fluoride salt, after X-rays showed it was there (Coster and Hevesy 1923); put hydrogen fluoride in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.hafnium_reduc: HfF4 + 2 Ca -> Hf + 2 CaF2: brittle hafnium powder; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.hafnium_cryst: Hafnium grown as a crystal bar from its iodide (van Arkel and de Boer 1925); put iodine in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.monazite_crac: Monazite baked in strong sulfuric acid: the rare earths dissolve as sulfates, the phosphate as phosphoric acid; put sulfuric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.cerium_separa: Cerium is oxidized and comes out first; the sulfate is ignited to ceria (Mosander 1839)
reaction.periodic_elements.lanthanum_sep: Lanthanum, the least soluble double salt, crystallizes next and is ignited to lanthana (Mosander 1839)
reaction.periodic_elements.praseodymium_: Didymium split by a hundred recrystallizations: green praseodymium (Auer von Welsbach 1885)
reaction.periodic_elements.neodymium_sep: And the pink new didymium, neodymium (Auer von Welsbach 1885)
reaction.periodic_elements.cerium_reduct: CeO2 + 2 Ca -> Ce + 2 CaO; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.lanthanum_red: La2O3 + 3 Ca -> 2 La + 3 CaO; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.praseodymium_: Pr6O11 + 11 Ca -> 6 Pr + 11 CaO; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.neodymium_red: Nd2O3 + 3 Ca -> 2 Nd + 3 CaO; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.residue_prota: Protactinium stays with the tantalum-like part of the roasted residue
reaction.periodic_elements.protactinium_: Protactinium carried down with tantalum and separated by its activity (Hahn and Meitner 1918)
reaction.periodic_elements.francium_prec: One actinium atom in a hundred decays to a new alkali metal; caesium salt carries it down (Perey 1939); put caesium chloride in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.scandium_exch: Scandium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.scandium_redu: Sc2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.yttrium_excha: Yttrium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.yttrium_reduc: Y2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.samarium_exch: Samarium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.samarium_redu: Sm2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.europium_exch: Europium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.europium_redu: Eu2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.gadolinium_ex: Gadolinium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.gadolinium_re: Gd2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.terbium_excha: Terbium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.terbium_reduc: Tb4O7 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.dysprosium_ex: Dysprosium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.dysprosium_re: Dy2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.holmium_excha: Holmium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.holmium_reduc: Ho2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.erbium_exchan: Erbium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.erbium_reduct: Er2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.thulium_excha: Thulium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.thulium_reduc: Tm2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.ytterbium_exc: Ytterbium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.ytterbium_red: Yb2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.lutetium_exch: Lutetium comes off the resin column in its own band and is ignited to the oxide (Spedding 1947)
reaction.periodic_elements.lutetium_redu: Lu2O3 reduced with calcium; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.xenotime_leac: Xenotime dissolved in hot hydrochloric acid: yttrium and the heavy rare earths as chlorides; put hydrochloric acid in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.ilmenite_chlo: 2 FeTiO3 + 7 Cl2 + 6 C -> 2 TiCl4 + 2 FeCl3 + 6 CO: chlorine over hot ilmenite and coke; put chlorine in the reagent slot and coke in the fuel slot
reaction.periodic_elements.rutile_chlori: TiO2 + 2 Cl2 + 2 C -> TiCl4 + 2 CO: rutile chlorinated with coke; put chlorine in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.kroll_reducti: TiCl4 + 2 Mg -> Ti + 2 MgCl2 under argon: titanium sponge (Kroll 1940); electrolyse the magnesium chloride back to magnesium; put magnesium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.aluminium_van: Aluminium melted with vanadium in the ratio 6 to 4: the master alloy for titanium; put vanadium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.titanium_allo: Titanium sponge melted with the master alloy into Ti-6Al-4V (1954); put aluminium-vanadium master alloy in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.uranium_hydro: Hydrogen fluoride gas over hot uranium oxide gives the green salt, UF4; put hydrogen fluoride in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.uranium_reduc: UF4 + 2 Mg -> U + 2 MgF2 in a sealed bomb: the Ames process made the uranium for the first reactor (1942); put magnesium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.silicon_cryst: A seed dipped in molten silicon and drawn slowly up grows one perfect crystal, sliced into wafers (Czochralski 1916, Teal 1950)
reaction.periodic_elements.germanium_cry: A molten zone swept along a germanium bar again and again carries the impurities to one end (Pfann 1952)
reaction.periodic_elements.diamond_synth: Graphite dissolved in molten nickel at 50,000 atmospheres crystallizes as diamond (General Electric 1954); put nickel in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.uranium_hexaf: UF4 + F2 -> UF6: fluorine turns the green salt into a white solid that boils off at 56 °C; put fluorine in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.uranium_enric: UF6 gas pumped through thousands of porous nickel barriers: the lighter uranium-235 creeps through a little faster (K-25 1945). One part of 3.5% fuel and six of 0.25% tails from seven of natural uranium
reaction.periodic_elements.depleted_uran: Depleted uranium hexafluoride reduced by magnesium: the dense metal of armour and penetrators; put magnesium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.fuel_conversi: Enriched UF6 and steam in a hydrogen stream give uranium dioxide powder; put a water bucket in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.fuel_pellet_s: Uranium dioxide powder pressed into pellets and sintered in hydrogen to a dense ceramic
reaction.periodic_elements.zircaloy.desc: Zirconium melted with 1.5% tin: Zircaloy lets neutrons through and stands hot water (Rickover's navy 1952); put tin in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.recovered_ura: Spent fuel dissolved in nitric acid; tributyl phosphate pulls the uranium out for reuse (PUREX 1954)
reaction.periodic_elements.plutonium_ext: Plutonium stripped from the solvent and ignited to the oxide (PUREX 1954)
reaction.periodic_elements.neptunium_ext: Neptunium follows the plutonium and is split off by its valence (McMillan and Abelson 1940)
reaction.periodic_elements.americium_ext: Americium stays in the acid with the fission products and is parted on resin (Seaborg 1944)
reaction.periodic_elements.curium_extrac: Curium comes off the resin just before americium (Seaborg, James and Ghiorso 1944)
reaction.periodic_elements.promethium_ex: Promethium parted from the fission products on an ion-exchange column (Marinsky, Glendenin and Coryell 1945)
reaction.periodic_elements.technetium_ex: Technetium-99, the first man-made element (Perrier and Segre 1937), is a kilogram-scale fission product: it is washed out as pertechnetate and reduced
reaction.periodic_elements.plutonium_red: PuO2 reduced with calcium in a sealed crucible; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.neptunium_red: NpO2 reduced with calcium in a sealed crucible; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.americium_red: AmO2 reduced with calcium in a sealed crucible; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.curium_reduct: Cm2O3 reduced with calcium in a sealed crucible; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.promethium_re: Pm2O3 reduced with calcium in a sealed crucible; put calcium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.astatine_synt: Bismuth bombarded with alpha particles gives astatine-211 (Corson, MacKenzie and Segre 1940); put helium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.berkelium_syn: Americium bombarded with alpha particles gives berkelium (Thompson, Ghiorso and Seaborg 1949); put helium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.californium_s: Curium bombarded with alpha particles gives californium (1950); put helium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.mendelevium_s: A billion einsteinium atoms bombarded with alpha particles gave 17 atoms of mendelevium, caught on gold foil (Ghiorso 1955); put helium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.calcium_48_se: Calcium ions bent round a magnet: the heavier calcium-48 lands in its own pocket (Lawrence's calutron, 1943); calcium-48 is boosted fivefold for play
reaction.periodic_elements.niobium_titan: Niobium melted with 47% titanium and drawn into wire that carries current with no resistance at 4 K (Westinghouse 1962); put titanium in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.integrated_ci: Silicon wafers oxidised, masked, etched and doped with boron, layer upon layer: a whole circuit on one chip (Kilby and Noyce 1959); put boron in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.gallium_arsen: Gallium and arsenic melted under boric oxide and pulled as one crystal: the stuff of LEDs, lasers and space solar cells (Holonyak 1962); put arsenic in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.iron_boron_al: Iron melted with 1.4% boron, the ratio of a neodymium magnet; put boron in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.neodymium_mag: Nd2Fe14B powder pressed in a magnetic field and sintered: the strongest permanent magnet (Sagawa 1984); put iron-boron alloy in the reagent slot
reaction.periodic_elements.boron_carbide: 4 B + C -> B4C at white heat: a ceramic nearly as hard as diamond; coke in the fuel slot gives the carbon
reaction.periodic_elements.nobelium_synt: Curium bombarded with carbon (Dubna and Berkeley 1958-66): a few atoms of nobelium, known only by the decay chain the detectors record; put carbon in the reagent slot
